title: Coordinate projection orientation equals the coefficient-unit integration mate
statement: For a finite purity setting P, a separated finite-type k-scheme Y and d >= 0, let z be the exact comparison image of diagonalAffineMate for the normalized projective-line transport at P.diagonalExponent, followed by diagonalDualizingComparison inverse. Identify the two recursive tower/projection pairs by their coordinate recursion. Then the inverse of the specified diagonalDualizingObject on p_d is z. This is only a coefficient-unit orientation equation; no arbitrary coefficient K and no ordered purity comparison occurs. The HEq specification of z uniquely fixes its arrow. This specializes the normalization of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], with the coordinates of [def-pur-projection-purity-coordinates].

source.place: Model diagonal/DNC integration normalization and final canonical reassociations.

proof.text: Identify the dependent recursive tower/projection pairs by induction. In the unique ordinary representative of the diagonal orientation, specialize its coordinate normalization to the identity chart, with the actual projective-line trace transport and datum. The two Tate pullback constraints cancel; cancel the common exceptional etale-locality comparison and use the identity pullback isomorphism to get e.inverse = diagonalAffineMate. The comparison-unit characterization of the orientation gives its inverse after exact site comparison. Rank zero and the empty scheme obey the same unit equations.

theorem projection_diagonal_unit_integration (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) (aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    [LocallyOfFiniteType aY] [QuasiCompact aY] [IsSeparated aY] (d : ℕ) :
    letI := (projection_geometry Y d).1
    letI := projection_smooth Y d
    (P.diagonalDualizingObject d (iteratedAffineLineProj Y d) aY).inv =
      projectionUnitIntegration P Y aY d
